newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may cut mthly devaluation rate in H2 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may cut mthly devaluation rate in H2 - paper.

text.p: Hungary may cut the forint's monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate to below one percent in the second half of 1997, depending on inflation and a national price-wage agreement, the Finance Ministry said.
Secretary of State Laszlo Akar was quoted on Wednesday by the daily Vilaggazdasag as saying that a cut in the devaluation rate may come if inflation continues to decline in the next few months.

A condition of a substantial reduction is an agreement between the government, the employers and the employees in the Interest Coordination Council about a slow rise in prices and wages in 1998, Akar said.

"If there is an agreement, and a substantial decline in inflation can be targeted, there is a good chance that the devaluation rate can be cut by more than 0.1 percentage points in the second half of the year," he said.

Akar spoke after trade minister Szabolcs Fazakas told a conference in New York that the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) planned to cut the devaluation rate to below one percent, and Hungary would not need monthly devaluations at all in 1998, the paper said.

However, NBH President Gyorgy Suranyi told Vilaggazdasag that the government's and the NBH's devaluation policies were unchanged and according to their latest decision, the monthly devaluation rate would be maximum 1.1 percent this year.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told Reuters earlier this week that the devaluation rate should be reduced for the second half of the year if the current inflation and foreign trade trends in the economy continue.

"If the trade account's position is very bad, I would not regard a devaluation rate cut good," Medgyessy said, adding that the trend reflected by the figures of the first few months of this year seemed to be positive.
